Sally: Next year, the city of Cambridge is planning to build a new highway that will run from the east part of the city to the west. The highway should relieve some of the traffic coming downtown from the suburbs. If things go as planned, construction will begin next summer.
Environmentalists' groups are protesting the construction of this new highway. They say that if the city decided to build it, the pollution level would increase exponentially. John Smits, you are the head of "Citizens for Green", a climate change activist group. How do you think we can avoid this environmental issue?

John Smits: The city could work on a better public transit system instead of planning more roads. If more people used buses, there would be less traffic and better air for us to breathe. The smog here will be as bad as in Boston if we go ahead with the proposed plan.

Sally: Can you tell us how you are going to put pressure on the city officials?
John Smits: We are organizing a protest in front of the city hall on Sunday.
Sally: What would you suggest to our listeners if they wanted to get more involved?
John Smits: If we want a better future for our children, we will need to make sure our air stays clean. I wouldn't choose parking lots over green spaces.

Conditional Sentences with If Clause

You use the first conditional with If clauses to talk about real possibilities in the future.

You use the second conditional to talk about unreal or imaginary (hypothetical) situations in the future.
You use the First Conditional to say it's possible that you will do or not do something. In that condition, something else may, will or will not happen.
The parts of the sentence are divided into two clauses: the If clause and the Condition clause.
You use the Second Conditional to talk about hypothetical situations. It's not certain that it's possible to fulfill the condition.

Example:
If I had a million dollars, I would buy a car.

Do you have a million dollars? No.
Is it possible to suddenly get a million dollars? Not really.
What would you do if you had a million dollars? Buy a car.

Modals for Suggestions
When you want to offer advice or give solutions to a problem, you use modals like might, should or could.
These modals can go at the beginning of the sentence, or after a clause starting with “If ...”.
The modal is followed by a verb in the base form. You do not use “to”.
